questions.title: Planning an experiment — coil, induced p.d. & frequency

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
Diagram: a thin coil (N turns, cross-sectional area A, length l) connected in series with a resistor S and an a.c. supply / signal generator; an oscilloscope connected in parallel with the resistor to display the p.d. V across it.
Procedure and measurements: vary the frequency f (independent variable) and measure the peak p.d. V across the resistor (dependent variable), keeping the peak supply voltage E constant. Determine V from the oscilloscope by multiplying the amplitude/height of the trace by the y-gain; determine f by measuring the time for one cycle (number of divisions × time-base) and using f = 1/T.
Analysis: plot a graph of 1/V against f (or f against 1/V, or lg V against lg f). The relationship is valid if a straight line through the origin is produced (for lg V against lg f, a straight line of gradient −1). From V = KAN²ES/(lf): gradient = l/(KAN²ES), so K = l/(gradient × AN²ES).
Controls: keep E, N, A, l and S constant. Determine A by measuring the coil diameter d with calipers/a micrometer (A = πd²/4), repeating at different positions and averaging. Measure l with a rule. Determine S with an ohmmeter (or a separate circuit with ammeter and voltmeter, S = V/I).
Safety: the coil/resistor may get hot — switch off the power supply between readings (or wear gloves) to prevent burns; allow the resistor to cool so S (and hence the conditions) stays constant.

questions.title: Analysis of data — resistors in parallel & internal e.m.f.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
E = I(R/n + Z), so 1/I = R/(En) + Z/E.
gradient = R/E and y-intercept = Z/E

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: Plot the six points of 1/I against 1/n (within half a small square), each with a vertical error bar.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: Draw a straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable line (steepest/shallowest line through all the error bars).

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer: gradient ≈ 7.9 × 10³ A⁻¹ (from Δy/Δx over more than half the line's length). Absolute uncertainty = gradient of best fit − gradient of worst acceptable line.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.answer: y-intercept ≈ 0.59 × 10³ A⁻¹ (substituting a point into y = mx + c). Uncertainty = difference between the two intercepts.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.answer:
E = 5.8 V (mean of 5.6 V and 6.0 V).
R = gradient × E = 7.9 × 10³ × 5.8 = 46 kΩ
Z = y-intercept × E = 0.59 × 10³ × 5.8 = 3.4 kΩ

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.answer:
% uncertainty in R = (Δgradient/gradient + ΔE/E) × 100, with ΔE = 0.2 V:
= (Δgradient/gradient + 0.2/5.8) × 100 ≈ 5 %
